Append or Overwrite a Single Column in $cell.meta

Source: R/add_meta_column.R
add_meta_column.Rd

Adds one new column to niches.obj$cell.meta from a named vector, or overwrites an existing column of the same name. All other columns in $cell.meta are preserved unchanged.

Use add_cell_meta instead when you want to replace the entire metadata table.

col.values must be a named vector whose names are cell barcodes. It must supply a value for every cell in niches.obj$cell.list. Extra names (cells not in $cell.list) are silently ignored.

If col.name already exists in $cell.meta, a message is emitted and the column is overwritten.

Usage

add_meta_column(
  niches.obj,
  col.name,
  col.values,
  rebuild.edge.meta = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

niches.obj

A NICHESObject.

col.name

Character scalar. Name of the column to add or overwrite.

col.values

Named vector. Names must be cell barcodes covering every cell in niches.obj$cell.list. The vector type determines the column type (character, numeric, integer, logical, factor).

rebuild.edge.meta

Logical. If TRUE (default), regenerates niches.obj$edge.meta via .build_edge_meta() so the new column appears as Sending.<col.name> / Receiving.<col.name> (and Joint.<col.name> for categorical types) on every edge.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), emits a message when overwriting an existing column and when aggregation slots may be stale.

Value

Updated NICHESObject.

See also

add_cell_meta to replace the full metadata table; add_neighborhood_composition and aggregate_NICHESObject to recompute stale aggregations.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_example)

# Add a new numeric column
scores <- setNames(
  runif(length(NICHESv2_example$cell.list)),
  NICHESv2_example$cell.list
)
obj.updated <- add_meta_column(NICHESv2_example,
                               col.name   = "quality.score",
                               col.values = scores)
head(obj.updated$cell.meta[, c("cell", "quality.score")])
#> Key: <cell>
#>       cell quality.score
#>     <char>         <num>
#> 1:  Cell_1    0.52791704
#> 2: Cell_10    0.05861411
#> 3: Cell_11    0.99706914
#> 4: Cell_12    0.14903547
#> 5: Cell_13    0.51855664
#> 6: Cell_14    0.84612005

# Overwrite an existing categorical column
new.types <- setNames(
  sample(c("TypeA", "TypeB"), length(NICHESv2_example$cell.list),
         replace = TRUE),
  NICHESv2_example$cell.list
)
obj.updated <- add_meta_column(NICHESv2_example,
                               col.name   = "celltype",
                               col.values = new.types)
#> [add_meta_column] Column "celltype" already exists in $cell.meta and will be overwritten.
# }
